author: human
request:
Feature request: visits can currently only be created, never corrected. Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-5 is narrowed: cancelling a booked visit stays out of scope,
  but correcting its date and description is now in. Record the narrowing
  the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The edit form is reachable by its URL alone: the owner detail page gains
  no edit link in this request. A visible entry point may come as a
  follow-up request.

Add editing for a booked visit:

- GET /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit shows the visit
  form prefilled with that visit's current date and description. Reuse the
  existing visit form template (pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm) and its `visit`
  model attribute.
- POST to the same URL validates like visit creation (description required,
  date in the future). On success it updates that visit in place — the pet
  must not gain an additional visit record — and redirects to the owner
  detail page. On validation failure it redisplays the form.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Correcting a booked visit's date and description
summary: A booked visit's date and description can be corrected on the visit itself. The correction form opens on the visit's current values, a correction is checked exactly as a booking is, and an accepted correction returns to the owner's record. The pet gains no second visit. Cancelling a booked visit stays out of scope.
acceptance_criteria: given a booked visit, when its correction form is opened, then the form shows that visit's current date and description
given a booked visit, when a description and a date later than today are submitted, then that visit carries the new values and the owner's record is shown
given a booked visit, when a correction is accepted, then the pet holds the same number of visits as before
given a blank description, when the correction is submitted, then it is refused and the description is named
given a date of today or earlier, when the correction is submitted, then it is refused and the date is named
given a refused correction, when the form is shown again, then it carries the submitted values and the reason for the refusal
edge case 1: a correction naming a visit that does not belong to the named pet, or a pet that does not belong to the named owner, is refused rather than applied
edge case 2: a correction leaves the visit on the same pet; a visit cannot be moved to another pet
non_goals: cancelling a booked visit (NG-5 keeps this row)
a visible entry point: no page links to the correction form in this slice
moving a corrected visit to another pet
notes: NG-5 narrowed in docs/prd.md and recorded in docs/adr/2026-08-17-non-goal-visit-correction.md; the 2026-08-08 non-goal ADR carries a forward pointer in its Status line. The ADR index row in docs/adr/README.md is outside product write scope and still needs adding by the ADR owner. Two questions the request left open are recorded in the PRD's Open Questions rather than consulted: whether a past visit can be corrected under the booking date rule, and which page would carry an entry point. No prd-autofix records to audit.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The slice extends an existing shape rather than opening new ground. Correcting a visit is the create-then-edit pair PetController already demonstrates (initUpdateForm/processUpdateForm), applied to the third level of the Owner aggregate: the write goes Owner -> Pet -> Visit and is persisted by OwnerRepository.save cascading, exactly as booking does (system-design.md Contracts, 'Invariants the rows cannot carry'; ADR 2026-07-31-feature-package-organization). Three small adjustments are needed, none of them a new pattern. First, VisitController's @ModelAttribute("visit") loader unconditionally constructs a Visit and calls pet.addVisit on it; the edit route must instead resolve the existing visit, or the pet gains a second visit record. Give the loader an optional visitId path variable (@PathVariable(name = "visitId", required = false) Integer visitId): absent, current behaviour is unchanged; present, it returns the visit already held by the pet and adds nothing. One loader keeps the owner and pet resolution, the model attributes, and the mass-assignment binder shared by both routes. Second, Pet exposes only getVisits(); it needs a by-identity accessor mirroring Owner.getPet(Integer) so the visit is reached through the aggregate rather than filtered in the controller. Third, the non-future-date rule already lives in processNewVisitForm; extract it to one private check both handlers call, so the controller still holds exactly one occurrence of the rule (architecture-principles.md pattern catalog, Web controller row: 'A new rule added to a controller is a fresh violation'). Binding the submitted values onto the loaded Visit instance and saving the owner produces an UPDATE, since the instance carries an id and is already in the pet's visit set; the count is unchanged with no re-add. The form template needs no change: it posts to the current URL with no th:action, and it already branches on visit['new'] for its heading. No new module, package, dependency, or persistence change. ADR index row for docs/adr/2026-08-17-non-goal-visit-correction.md added, as the product expert flagged.

Pet gains a by-identity visit accessor; no repository is added, and OwnerRepository stays the sole write path for the graph
the corrected visit is written by cascade from Owner, so no schema, mapping, or vendor-script change is involved

findings.description: This test's premise does not match the code it exercises. Visit (src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/owner/Visit.java) has no petId property at all -- only date and description. Spring's DataBinder silently drops a request parameter with no matching bean property, so .param("petId", String.valueOf(anotherPet.getId())) never reaches any binding target and is a complete no-op. The test would pass identically even if a real 'move visit to another pet' vulnerability existed, because there is no petId field for a fix to guard and no code path for a regression to break. A test whose failure can never point at a real defect does not belong in the suite (tested-as-spec). Either drop the vacuous parameter/comment and let the existing 'belongs to another pet' refusal test (already present) stand as edge case 2's coverage, or rewrite this test to probe a binding vector that actually exists on Visit.

Pet.getVisit(Integer) is new pure domain logic with no I/O or framework dependency, but it is exercised only indirectly through VisitControllerTests (a Spring MVC integration test). testing-principles.md SS Test Pyramid: 'A reviewer applies this by asking of each new rule: could this have been tested without booting the framework? If yes, it belongs in a unit.' jacoco confirms the gap: Pet.java is at 85% line / 83% branch coverage with 1 of 4 branches on the `!visit.isNew() && Objects.equals(visit.getId(), id)` line missed -- there is no test exercising a pet holding both a persisted and an unpersisted (new, id-null) visit. Add a dedicated unit test class (e.g. PetTests) covering getVisit directly: match on an existing id, a missing id, and a new visit that must not be matched by id.

`Pet anotherPet = new Pet();` calls the production constructor directly. testing-principles.md SS Test Data Construction: 'Tests never call production constructors directly... A slice adding a test writes it behind [a factory] from the start.' This file already establishes the pattern with its own bookedVisit() factory; the touched init() fixture in this same diff also continues constructing Owner/Pet directly and should move behind a factory (e.g. createAPet()) while it is being touched.

author: change-grader
summary: add in-place correction of a booked visit

blast_radius.note: Nine files in one module and one package: two production classes (76 lines), two test classes, five docs. No sensitive paths, no dependency, schema or template change. The only reach beyond the new route is the shared @ModelAttribute loader and the extracted date check, both of which the existing booking route runs through and the pre-existing booking tests still cover.

semantic_surprise.note: Read every hunk. The loader's visitId == null branch reproduces the previous body exactly, the extracted rejectDateNotInFuture is character-identical to the code it replaces, and the correction binds onto the instance already in the pet's visit set rather than a fresh Visit, so no phantom record appears. Pet.getVisit guards on !isNew() before comparing ids, so an unbooked visit with a null id cannot be resolved as the correction target. Nothing behaves differently from what the diff advertises.

test_adequacy.note: The tests are real, not tautological: they assert on the actual pet instance the controller mutated, pin the typeMismatch.visitDate error code, verify save is never called on a refusal, and would fail against a broken loader. But the slice's central invariant, that the pet gains no second visit, is proven only in memory against a @MockitoBean OwnerRepository; nothing exercises the JPA merge that has to produce an UPDATE rather than an INSERT, while the analogous booking path does hold that coverage in ClinicServiceTests.shouldAddNewVisitForPet (@DataJpaTest).

reviewer_hedging.note: All four roster reviewers approved with empty findings in round 2, but the security reviewer carried two recommendations forward, one of them substantive: processVisitCorrectionForm takes @ModelAttribute Owner and then saves it, so a POST to the new edit URL carrying firstName, address, city or telephone rewrites the owner's details. The reviewer judged it baseline parity with processNewVisitForm and the open /owners/{id}/edit route rather than a new grant, which reading the code confirms, but it now rides a second endpoint and no test pins it. The unrun NVD supply-chain check is the second, and the slice touches no dependency.

scope_deviation.note: The diff matches the PRD file targets, the owner detail page gains no edit link exactly as the owner decided, and the docs changes are the NG-5 narrowing the owner ordered, recorded through the project's own non-goal ADR convention. The one design revision was an autofix-audit re-triage that vouched for two ADR paths and explicitly left the design assessment unchanged. The row's build_retries of 0 understates history: two build-failure records at lines 7 and 8 precede the superseding design-block and reset the counter, but their cause was that same doc-vouching bookkeeping, not scope drift.

rationale: Correct and contained: the booking path is behavior-identical and the correction updates in place. Two residuals deserve a read before merge. The no-second-visit invariant is proven only against a mocked repository, and the new edit POST binds and saves the whole Owner, so it can rewrite owner details. Both are parity with existing code, neither is pinned by a test.
